audits.title: An audit of high-dose and combination antipsychotic prescribing across the general adult inpatient wards in Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
audits.standard: Trust recommendations for high-dose antipsychotic therapy (HDAT) monitoring and clozapine consideration
audits.setting: Eight general adult inpatient wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 21/121 on combination therapy, 11 on HDAT (9%); clozapine considered in 9 of 11 HDAT patients; ECG before HDAT 100% but after dose increase only 36%; baseline prolactin 46%, HbA1c 91%.

audits.other_findings: Clozapine considered in 13 of 21 on combination therapy but only 2 started. HDAT prevalence lower than the 28% POMH 2012 figure.
audits.citation: Hyland D, Hemmings B, Elagamy Y. An audit of high-dose and combination antipsychotic prescribing across the general adult inpatient wards in Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S82-S83.

audits.title: Audit on High Dose Antipsychotic Treatment (HDAT) Monitoring at Rampton Hospital
audits.standard: HDAT monitoring guidelines (MHRA/Committee on Safety of Medicines): bloods, ECG and observations after each dose escalation and 6-monthly; consent documentation
audits.setting: Rampton Hospital, high secure setting, Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Blood and ECG monitoring 8% to 23%; yearly TFT 88% and prolactin 72%; quarterly observations 77%.

cycle2.result: 6% of patients on HDAT (18); quarterly bloods about 50-60%, quarterly ECG about 40%; yearly TFT 100%, prolactin 71%; quarterly observations 100% (regular HDAT), 81% (including PRN); consent forms 100%.

audits.other_findings: Reasons for treatment documented in 85% on regular HDAT. Prescribers reminded of guidelines; re-audit planned 2021-22.
audits.citation: Das A, Yanson I. Audit on High Dose Antipsychotic Treatment (HDAT) Monitoring at Rampton Hospital. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S182-S183.

audits.title: Audit of high dose antipsychotics (HDA) prescribing on high dependency unit (HDU) and acute ward, Nepean Mental Health Centre, Nepean Blue Mountains Local Health District, Sydney, Australia
audits.standard: Individual and combined antipsychotic doses within recommended maximum (TGA, Medsafe, Therapeutic Guidelines): target 100%
audits.setting: High dependency unit and acute ward, Nepean Mental Health Centre, Sydney

cycle1.result: 13/30 (43.3%) on >100% of cumulative maximum dose; 3 (10%) above maximum for regular antipsychotics; 0/30 above maximum for PRN.

audits.citation: Jawad A, Mikes-Liu K, Mah C, Roy K. Audit of high dose antipsychotics (HDA) prescribing on high dependency unit (HDU) and acute ward, Nepean Mental Health Centre, Nepean Blue Mountains Local Health District, Sydney, Australia. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S328-S328.

audits.title: High dose antipsychotic treatment monitoring audit
audits.standard: Trust guidance: patients on high dose antipsychotic treatment (HDAT) should have a HDAT monitoring form plus physical health assessment
audits.setting: Assertive Outreach Team, Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Four patients on HDAT (117-150% of maximum BNF dose); only one had a HDAT form and it was out of date; 39/52 (75%) had a physical health assessment in the past 12 months

audits.other_findings: Two of the 13 without a physical health assessment were on HDAT; barriers were poor team awareness of HDAT, no reliable reminder system and insufficient equipment.
audits.citation: Scott J, Belda J. High dose antipsychotic treatment monitoring audit. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S348-S348.

audits.title: Audit of high dose antipsychotic prescribing in the havering community recovery team
audits.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists consensus: high-dose antipsychotic prescribing as an explicit time-limited trial with regular review and safety monitoring
audits.setting: Havering Community Recovery Team, North East London Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 16/349 (4.58%) on high-dose antipsychotics; 0/16 had monitoring form available; 12 (75%) had documented review; 4 (25%) had no documented review

audits.other_findings: Recommended staff education, better care plan documentation and wider availability of monitoring forms with pharmacy.
audits.citation: Umeh C, Ionita S. Audit of high dose antipsychotic prescribing in the havering community recovery team. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S354-S355.

audits.title: Audit of High Dose Antipsychotic Therapy (HDAT) Prescribing Among Inpatients in East Suffolk
audits.standard: BNF and Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines antipsychotic dosage; HDAT monitoring form for each patient on HDAT

cycle1.result: 166 (64.6%) on antipsychotics; 2 (1.2%) discharged on HDAT, of whom one did not have the monitoring form completed.

audits.other_findings: HDAT prescribing was less prevalent than assumed.
audits.citation: Ruhi S, Alase A, Aregbesola M, Khan Q, Rizvi F. Audit of High Dose Antipsychotic Therapy (HDAT) Prescribing Among Inpatients in East Suffolk. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S214-S214. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.530.

audits.title: Reducing high dose antipsychotic therapy (HDAT) in a community mental health team (CMHT)
audits.standard: RCPsych consensus statement CR190; seven best practice audit criteria (Humber NHS Foundation Trust)
audits.setting: Community mental health team (affiliations University College Dublin and Galway University Hospital)

cycle1.result: 68% prescribed antipsychotics and 9% on HDAT; no patient met all seven criteria.

cycle2.result: 177/246 (72%) on antipsychotics; 14 (8%) on HDAT; no patient met all seven criteria but adherence better overall.

audits.other_findings: Blood and ECG monitoring were the most consistently measured parameters.
audits.citation: Walsh R, Patel S, Loddo V, Fahy R, Walsh E. Reducing high dose antipsychotic therapy (HDAT) in a community mental health team (CMHT). BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S110-S111.

audits.title: Prescribing and Monitoring of High Dose Antipsychotic Therapy (HDAT) in the Acute Inpatient Setting
audits.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists HDAT guidance: documented rationale, risk-benefit discussion or capacity/legal process, and ECG, BMI and blood monitoring
audits.setting: Three acute general adult inpatient wards, Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 3/49 (6%) on HDAT, with no documented rationale and variable physical health monitoring

audits.intervention: Education sessions for rotational junior doctors in the six months after the initial audit

cycle2.result: 11/47 (23%) on HDAT; only 2 of 7 MDT/consultant-initiated cases noted HDAT initiation; 8 had ECG within a month before HDAT; only 3 had repeat ECG within 7 days

audits.other_findings: Three patients gained at least 5 kg on HDAT; teaching had limited impact due to doctor turnover. Planned: departmental teaching, HDAT stickers on medication charts and ward round template.
audits.citation: Buston G, Kay H, Nwibe I, Edge O, Sparasci O, Sindhi A. Prescribing and Monitoring of High Dose Antipsychotic Therapy (HDAT) in the Acute Inpatient Setting. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(Suppl 1):S160-S160.

audits.title: Prevalence and correlates of "high dose" antipsychotic prescribing: findings from a hospital audit.
audits.standard: High dose defined as prescribed daily dose/defined daily dose ratio above 1.5
audits.setting: Inpatients, regional tertiary psychiatric hospital, Benin City
audits.other_findings: Predictors were diagnosis, polypharmacy, previous admission and anticholinergic use.

audits.title: Antipsychotic prescribing for vulnerable populations: a clinical audit at an acute Australian mental health unit at two-time points.
audits.standard: Clinical guideline recommendations for antipsychotic monotherapy at minimum effective dose
audits.setting: Acute inpatient mental health unit, Brisbane

cycle1.result: Sub-optimal polytherapy and high-dose prescribing identified; overall 62.5% of 400 patients discharged on a single antipsychotic within recommended dose range.

audits.intervention: Preliminary findings and education sessions provided to physicians between cohorts.

cycle2.result: Sub-optimal polytherapy and high-dose rates persisted; education programme alone was ineffective.

audits.other_findings: Involuntary treatment, frequent hospitalisations and previous clozapine use increased risk of polytherapy and high-dose prescribing.
audits.citation: McMillan SS, Jacobs S, Wilson L, Theodoros T, Robinson G, Anderson C, et al.. Antipsychotic prescribing for vulnerable populations: a clinical audit at an acute Australian mental health unit at two-time points. BMC Psychiatry. 2017;17(1):139. doi:10.1186/s12888-017-1295-1. PMID: 28407747.

audits.title: Prevalence of High-dose Antipsychotic Prescribing in Schizophrenia: A Clinical Audit in a Regional Queensland Mental Health Service.
audits.standard: International guidelines and local policy (December 2017) on antipsychotic monotherapy at minimum effective dose
audits.setting: Regional Queensland mental health service, Central Queensland Hospital and Health Service, community and inpatient

cycle1.result: 15% prescribed high doses; 20% prescribed polytherapy; 85% prescribed within the dose range.

audits.other_findings: Individual psychiatrists' prescribing practices were also examined.
audits.citation: Luthra S, Duggan L, Agrawal A, Kaur G, Luthra N. Prevalence of High-dose Antipsychotic Prescribing in Schizophrenia: A Clinical Audit in a Regional Queensland Mental Health Service. Int J Appl Basic Med Res. 2023;13(2):70-76. doi:10.4103/ijabmr.ijabmr_504_22. PMID: 37614838.

audits.title: Antipsychotic Polypharmacy and High-Dose Antipsychotics in Involuntary Patients: a Seven-Year Audit of Discharge Prescriptions in an Acute Care Unit.
audits.standard: Antipsychotic polypharmacy and high-dose antipsychotic rates as quality of prescribing indicators
audits.setting: Acute care unit, psychiatry department of Leiria district hospital

cycle1.result: Antipsychotic polypharmacy in 70.5% and high-dose antipsychotics in 51.4% of involuntary patients at discharge.

audits.other_findings: Polypharmacy strongly associated with long-acting injectables (OR 28.29) and male gender.
audits.citation: Martinho S, Poças A, Simões M, Laureano C. Antipsychotic Polypharmacy and High-Dose Antipsychotics in Involuntary Patients: a Seven-Year Audit of Discharge Prescriptions in an Acute Care Unit. Psychiatr Q. 2021;92(1):1-14. doi:10.1007/s11126-020-09762-1. PMID: 32430698.
